prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate objective function for a GNN-based netlist tier-partitioner (2-tier 3D IC).
Hypothesis of the change: The locality term's per-edge weight normalisation by w_edge.sum() makes the term's effective pull depend on how many critical pairs exist; normalising by the number of edges (a constant, case-relative) and modestly raising the coefficient to 0.30 (x2) stabilises the term across circuits so C1 keeps its crit_cross gain without C2/C3 regression.
Rule-based digest (scores are improvement ratios vs. the official baseline; C1..C3 are the training circuits by size):
total=-0.003 robust(mean-std)=-0.009 min_case=-0.011 seed_std=0.019 tns_mean=-0.003 all_valid=True
  C1: score=+0.001 dWNS=+2.3% dTNS=-1.3% per-seed=[-0.03 +0.00 +0.03]
  C2: score=+0.008 dWNS=+1.1% dTNS=+0.5% per-seed=[+0.02 -0.00 +0.01]
  C3: score=-0.011 dWNS=-1.7% dTNS=-0.2% per-seed=[+0.00 +0.01 -0.04]
  partition stats vs baseline:
  C1: cut 137->138, wcut 421->424, crit_cross 0.011->0.011, repair_flips 103->102, changed-vs-baseline 1.4%
  C2: cut 318->319, wcut 1007->1007, crit_cross 0.000->0.000, repair_flips 238->240, changed-vs-baseline 2.6%
  C3: cut 582->575, wcut 1955->1937, crit_cross 0.069->0.081, repair_flips 353->352, changed-vs-baseline 1.4%
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID, first classify the failure (crash / non-finite loss / balance repair failure / timeout) and whether it is systematic or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which circuit/metric moved and the plausible mechanism (cut nets, critical-pair cross-tier, repair flips)? (3) is the seed spread acceptable? (4) one concrete next step. No preamble.

response:
(1) No. The normalisation change did not stabilise the term: C1 gained only +0.001 (crit_cross flat at 0.011, cut 137→138), C2 +0.008, but C3 regressed -0.011 with crit_cross rising 0.069→0.081 and wcut 1955→1937 — the opposite of the intended effect.

(2) C3 moved most: fewer cut nets but more critical-pair crossings and slightly fewer repair flips, suggesting the constant-normalised pull is too weak relative to repair on the largest circuit, letting crit pairs cross.

(3) Seed spread is marginal: C1 [-0.03,+0.03], C3 [-0.04,+0.01], seed_std 0.019 vs total -0.003 — noise dominates signal.

(4) Next: sweep coefficient 0.30→0.45 on C3 only, or normalise by critical-pair count rather than edge count, before full retrain.
